Abdullah bin Ubai rebuffed the Prophet's preaching; the Prophet excused him, for Muslims were then ordered to forgive the pagans and People of the Scripture until fighting was permitted.
Umar held back from punishing Uyaina when Al-Hurr recited the order to hold to forgiveness and leave the foolish; Ibn az-Zubair said it concerns forgiving people's misbehaviour.
In a dream the Prophet saw people half handsome and half ugly, who had mixed good and bad deeds, made wholly handsome in a river, for Allah forgave them.
All sins are forgiven except those whose doers expose what Allah screened, and on the Day Allah will make a believer confess his sins, then forgive what He had screened.
Visiting sick Sa'd before Badr, the Prophet preached to a mixed gathering, was rebuffed by Abdullah bin Ubai and excused him, as Muslims then forgave pagans and Scripture people.
The Prophet asked Allah to forgive his mistakes, ignorance and excess, his jest and earnest, what he did deliberately or not, past and future, secret and open.
Allah forgives the Prophet's followers the evil their souls whisper as long as they do not act on it or speak it.
A man who asked for a legal punishment was not questioned, and after praying with the Prophet was told Allah had forgiven his sin.
Uyaina accused Umar of giving too little and judging unjustly, but Umar held back when Al-Hurr recited the verse bidding forgiveness and turning from the foolish, keeping to Allah's Book.
Allah forgave a man who had his body burned and the ashes scattered out of fear of Him, and forgives a slave who sins and asks forgiveness again and again.
